references.text: The parallel account in [ref:Mark 12:41-44|Mark 12:41-44], where Jesus sits opposite the temple treasury and watches the crowd putting money into it. Mark gives the most detailed version of this event, including the widow's gift.
In [ref:2 Kings 12:9-10|2 Kings 12:9-10], a chest at the temple is described where people placed their gifts, which forms the background for the temple treasury (gazofulakion) mentioned here in Luke.

Just before this account, Jesus warns against the scribes who "devour widows' houses" ([ref:Luke 20:45-47|Luke 20:45-47]). The contrast between the rich and the poor widow in the following verse reinforces this message.

In [ref:Matthew 6:2-4|Matt 6:2-4], Jesus teaches about giving gifts in secret, as opposed to those who do it to be seen by others. The giving of the rich in the temple can be viewed in light of this teaching on the motivation behind generosity.

[ref:Deut 16:17|Deut 16:17] states that everyone should give according to their ability, based on the blessing the Lord has given. This principle underlies Jesus' observation of those who gave into the temple treasury.

In [ref:1 Chron 29:3-9|1 Chron 29:3-9], David and the leaders give generously to the temple from their own wealth. The generosity of the rich in the temple recalls this tradition of giving to God's house.
